newsitem.title: INDIA: India's ONGC up 7.0 pct after govt move.
newsitem.headline: India's ONGC up 7.0 pct after govt move.

text.p: India's state-run Oil & Natural Gas Corporation of India (ONGC) shares rose 12.75 rupees or 6.9 percent to 197.75 rupees at the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) on Friday after the government spoke of changes in oil policy, dealers said.
The Indian government on Friday said it will announce a new exploration policy within two months in which companies will be paid international prices for crude.
Domestic crude is currently priced at about $11 to $12 a barrel compared to $22 to $23 in international markets.
ONGC accounts for almost 90 percent of India's oil and gas production.
A cabinet panel of the government on Wednesday approved a proposal to revise crude oil price paid to ONGC and Oil India Ltd to 1,991 rupees per tonne from 1,741 rupees.
Oil analysts said ONGC would get marginal relief following the government's decision to raise prices of indigenous crude.
